leaders.name: Odrik Sluice
leaders.angle: Agricultural infrastructure and the political power of maintenance crews, rather than celebrated masterworks.
leaders.backstory: Odrik inherited a canal district whose magnificent ancient pumps had stopped because nobody remembered how to service them. He replaced their ingenious but irreplaceable mechanisms with plain golems that any village mason could mend. Farmers rewarded him with authority over their water schedules, and his maintenance crews gradually became a government crossing several guild jurisdictions. He will sell grain to either side of a war, but closes the sluices of anyone who tries to make his crews into soldiers.

Wearing a deep teal waxed canal-master's jacket with rust edging and broad shoulder cape, he actively turns a brass sluice wheel beside a glass water gauge at chest height. Stone canal locks and a squat clay maintenance golem behind him; sober daylight and blunt practical concentration.

leaders.hand_activity: Turning a small brass sluice wheel while watching the water level rise inside its glass channel.
leaders.clothing: A deep teal waxed canal-master's jacket with rust edging, heavy rolled cuffs and a broad waterproof shoulder cape.

leaders.name: Kelna Brasshear
leaders.angle: The ethics and safety of enchantment, without assuming every golem has Barnaxus's exceptional personhood.
leaders.backstory: Kelna learned to diagnose failing enchantments by listening to the uneven hum inside a golem's chest. After a workshop accident, she discovered that a celebrated master had concealed a spirit-binding inside an otherwise ordinary laborer's frame. She insisted that the bound being be released and that every workshop publish what its animating spells actually contained. Apprentices and cautious householders have since formed a faction around her demand that mastery include responsibility for what answers when a maker gives an order.
leaders.portrait: Young adult Luchuirp dwarf woman with pale freckled round face, short black curls and keen hazel eyes. Rich violet short scholar's mantle over a copper-colored diagnostic apron. She turns a tiny screwdriver in a bronze golem core with one hand while pressing a listening funnel to it with the other; rune workshop, restrained violet glimmer, patient scientific absorption.
leaders.primary_palette: Rich violet with copper accents
leaders.hand_activity: Tuning a golem core with a tiny screwdriver while pressing a listening funnel against it with the other hand.
leaders.clothing: A rich violet short scholar's mantle over a copper-colored leather diagnostic apron, close cuffs and a row of delicate instruments.

leaders.name: Vorra Rentshaper
leaders.angle: A dark Luchuirp offshoot turns the obedient servant economy into permanent dependence on its owners.
leaders.backstory: Vorra rescued several indebted workshops by buying their golems and leasing the same servants back to them. Each repair introduced another proprietary enchantment, until an entire district could neither harvest nor build without her permission. When its council challenged her fees, she recalled every leased construct on the morning the flood defenses needed reinforcement. The council submitted, and her creditor cities now call submission to her contracts the price of civilization.
leaders.portrait: Older Luchuirp dwarf woman with severe broad olive face, sleek iron-gray hair and heavy brows. Structured wine-red velvet merchant coat, high ivory collar, rigid shoulders and brass chain fastenings. With a tight closed smile she turns a bronze command key inside the shoulder lock of a foreground golem while pinning a rental contract flat with her other hand; shadowed warehouse of obedient constructs, cold polished wealth.
leaders.primary_palette: Wine red with ivory accents
leaders.hand_activity: Turning a command key inside a golem's shoulder lock while her other palm pins a rental contract to the desk.
leaders.clothing: A structured wine-red velvet merchant coat with tall ivory collar, rigid shoulders and rows of brass chain fastenings.

leaders.name: Durn Pell
leaders.angle: A survivor's insistence on shelters and manual safeguards challenges the civilization's dependence on enchantment.
leaders.backstory: Durn was a shelter mason when a hostile dispelling left his settlement's enchanted doors open during a raid. He saved its children through an unfinished service tunnel and spent the following winter designing gates that living hands could close. His fortified workshops still employ golems, but every essential system has an unenchanted second means of operation. Border towns follow him because he promises neither perfect machines nor another retreat beneath the world, only the chance to survive when a marvel fails.
leaders.portrait: Late-middle-aged Luchuirp dwarf man with dark umber skin, broken nose, close white beard and scar through one eyebrow. Golden-ocher mason's coat over slate-blue quilted armor with reinforced elbows. He tightens a heavy iron gate bolt with a short wrench while bracing the latch with his other hand; sunlit fortified surface workshop and stone emergency doorway, stubborn protective concentration, no magic.

leaders.hand_activity: Tightening a heavy gate bolt with a short iron wrench while bracing the latch with his other hand.
leaders.clothing: A golden-ocher mason's coat over slate-blue quilted armor, reinforced leather elbow guards and thick working gloves.

leaders.name: Sereia Coil-of-Law
leaders.angle: A lamia administrator examines the uneasy boundary between accommodation and the confederacy's informal racial castes.
leaders.backstory: Sereia was trained as a court mage but made her reputation rewriting contracts that assumed every citizen walked on two legs. Her registries gave lamia households, centaur companies, and human guilds enforceable places in the same administration. Those categories also hardened into rules about which peoples could hold which offices, a restriction she defends as the necessary scaffolding of peace. The officials who support her want the confederacy to survive an absent king, even if its citizens must fit more neatly into her ledgers.
leaders.portrait: Mature female lamia, warm-brown human face, subtle emerald temple and neck scales, long dark braids, amber eyes and visible arc of green scaled tail at the lower edge. Royal cobalt high-necked registrar's robe with silver geometric shoulder panels. She draws a branching registry diagram on a parchment map with a silver stylus while guiding a dividing ruler with her other hand; monumental archive, exacting civic composure.
leaders.primary_palette: Royal cobalt with silver accents
leaders.hand_activity: Drawing a branching registry diagram on a parchment map with a silver stylus while guiding a dividing ruler with the other hand.
leaders.clothing: A royal cobalt high-necked registrar's robe with silver geometric shoulder panels and a narrow ceremonial sash.

leaders.name: Torven Longstride
leaders.angle: A centaur frontier commander gives the outlying settlements a political voice independent of the great cities.
leaders.backstory: Torven spent twenty years defending settlements whose brightest children and richest harvests departed for the core cities. When an evacuation order abandoned three allied villages, he held the road until their people could follow. The villages elected him to carry a joint petition, and the centaur companies refused to replace him when the royal clerks dismissed it. He remains loyal to the confederacy, but insists that citizenship include the right to influence decisions made behind distant city walls.
leaders.portrait: Older male centaur, weathered tawny human face, salt-and-pepper hair at the nape, broad shoulders and chestnut equine withers visible below the torso. Sage-green travel poncho over a bronze scale chest panel. Both hands bind differently colored village ribbons together around a road spear's shaft, making a shared standard; open grassland and distant metropolis, weathered inclusive determination.

leaders.hand_activity: Binding several village ribbons together around a road spear's shaft, deliberately making one shared standard.

leaders.name: Ilyra Roof-Singer
leaders.angle: An urban harpy faction brings the city above street level into politics, mixing civic culture with extralegal resistance.
leaders.backstory: Ilyra organized the harpy messengers who nested above a city that taxed their deliveries but refused to recognize their homes. A landlord's attempt to tear down the high quarter became a week of vanished rent chests and mocking songs delivered through every upper window. Her couriers now protect rooftop markets, smuggle dissidents between districts, and maintain the fastest warning network in the confederacy. She bargains with the city below as its indispensable neighbor, never as its obedient ornament.
leaders.portrait: Adult harpy woman, sharp expressive tawny human face, copper-brown feather crest, broad feathered wings rising behind the shoulders, feathered forearms ending in dexterous clawed hands. Cropped burnt-orange courier vest, turquoise scarf and light leather harness. She pries up a foreground roof tile with one clawed hand and retrieves a hidden folded message with the other; tiled roofs and hanging gardens, irreverent conspiratorial grin.

leaders.hand_activity: Prying up a loose roof tile with one clawed hand while retrieving a hidden folded message with the other.

leaders.name: Avar Senn
leaders.angle: An authoritarian merchant preserves the multiracial metropolis while making its promise of asylum a source of exploitation.
leaders.backstory: Avar rose by supplying food and housing to newcomers whom the royal administration had welcomed faster than it could accommodate. He converted those emergency advances into hereditary obligations, then purchased offices that let him decide when a family had repaid them. His city admits almost anyone and displays every people of Erebus in its splendid public processions. Behind that hospitality, his magistrates make leaving one's assigned work far harder than entering the gates.

Warm ivory silk civic gown with broad imperial-purple lapels and pleated sleeves. He slides a citizenship token toward the viewer with one hand while crossing out an exit clause on the accompanying contract with his other hand; opulent balcony, distant procession banners, welcoming smile and silken predatory assurance.

leaders.name: Meren Glasshand
leaders.angle: A civic skeptic questions rule by personal supernatural charisma without abandoning the confederacy's pluralism.
leaders.backstory: Meren investigated a neighborhood magistrate who had used a charm to turn public consultations into unanimous acclaim. Exposure earned her a shattered hand and a new following among citizens uneasy about the court's almost religious reverence for its boy-king. Her assemblies require testimony outside magical influence and publish dissent beside the winning decision. She asks whether a people held together by one extraordinary ruler can learn to trust its ordinary disagreements.

leaders.name: Saeril Reedkeeper
leaders.angle: The material economy of a forest civilization: seed reserves, seasonal obligations, and the leverage of food.
leaders.backstory: Saeril kept the seed exchanges between groves whose nobles considered accounting beneath an elf's dignity. When blight destroyed an autumn harvest, his unglamorous reserves fed households that the court's songs had not remembered to count. The groves accepted his common calendar of planting, loans, and repayment, giving their steward influence that neither birth nor magic had earned him. He now trades that influence for secure borders and favorable treaties, regarding a glorious war as a particularly wasteful kind of famine.

leaders.name: Nethra Cinderbough
leaders.angle: Reconstruction and skilled adaptation after forest destruction, rather than vengeance or royal ritual.
leaders.backstory: Nethra returned from border service to find that a magical fire had spared her village's roots and destroyed nearly everything above them. She persuaded its survivors to build around the scarred trunks instead of abandoning them or demanding impossible restoration. Her bridges, cisterns, and sheltered nurseries made the damaged grove habitable while new growth slowly returned. Other burned communities now seek her leadership, and she measures victory by how many people can come home after the soldiers leave.

leaders.name: Iovain Stillroot
leaders.angle: A cruel Seelie ecological absolutism, distinct from the Svartalfar court's intrigue and predation.
leaders.backstory: Iovain tended a sacred grove through decades of rebuilding and came to regard every cleared field as another wound in the world's recovery. He began planting boundary trees across neighboring farms, preaching that the forest's return outweighed the claims of short-lived peoples. When hungry refugees cut those saplings for firewood, his followers drove them out and consecrated their abandoned houses as shrines. He offers the Ljosalfar an endless summer purchased by treating everyone beyond its shade as expendable.

leaders.name: Aelwen Many-Vows
leaders.angle: Elven longevity becomes an obligation to remember mortal allies rather than grounds for indifference to them.
leaders.backstory: Aelwen was sent to renew a treaty and discovered that three generations of its human signatories had died while her court delayed an answer. She stayed to record their names and found that their descendants remembered elven silence more clearly than elven promises. Her traveling witnesses now carry the histories of mortal allies between groves, insisting that an oath cannot wait upon the convenience of the long-lived. Border households and younger elves have made her the voice of those who must share a world before they can afford to understand it.

leaders.name: Namar Oathmolt
leaders.angle: A counter-enchanter protects the forest from benevolent and hostile magic alike, limiting even his own court's mages.
leaders.backstory: Namar once strengthened the spells that encouraged a frontier grove to grow, until competing enchantments left its trees flowering and dying in the same week. Undoing the damage taught him to prize limits more than displays of power. His wardens now inspect foreign relics, royal experiments, and druidic blessings with the same suspicion, earning enemies among allies who believe good intentions should exempt them. Groves tired of becoming somebody else's magical answer support his austere promise that their seasons will remain their own.

leaders.name: Brunna Chalkvein
leaders.angle: Dwarven caution serves public refuge and disaster preparation, rather than royal authority or mercantile expansion.
leaders.backstory: Brunna commanded a mine rescue when a spring thaw flooded workings that three feuding clans each claimed were another's responsibility. She cut through a private vault wall to reach the trapped crews, then submitted herself to the compensation court beside the people she had saved. The settlement established a common emergency fund and gave its administration to her. Her shelter towns admit outsiders during disasters under strict inventories and shared duties, making measured trust a matter of engineering rather than sentiment.

Vermilion rescue captain's coat with cream shoulder markings and broad leather braces. She actively swings a bronze alarm bell with one hand while directing an evacuation with a decisive open-palmed sweep of the other; reinforced stone floodgate shelter, warm lamplight, commanding reassuring urgency.

leaders.hand_activity: Swinging a bronze alarm bell outward with one hand while directing an evacuation with a decisive open-palmed sweep of the other.

leaders.name: Dorrik Ledgergrave
leaders.angle: A Khazad moral philosopher twists the vault's promise of security into a doctrine that prices people by their assets.
leaders.backstory: Dorrik began as an arbitrator asked to decide how much a collapsed mine owed its dead workers' families. His tables of compensation became a general theory that a person's claim to protection should equal the wealth they preserved for the hold. Rich clans endowed his school, while debtors found that even an honest accident could reduce their descendants' standing. His creditor faction keeps full vaults and orderly streets by making poverty evidence that a dwarf deserves less of both.

He sets a tiny worker figurine on one pan of a balance while adding gold weights to the other, studying it with grave pitiless calculation; geometrically ordered vault alcove, low amber light.

leaders.name: Helvi Handseer
leaders.angle: The runewarden tradition and contested ancestral memory, including the histories prestigious clans would erase.
leaders.backstory: Helvi lost her sight after years reading the ancestral pillars by candlelight and learned the old runewardens' art of knowing a history by touch. While restoring a damaged hall, she found that the names of banished kin had been chiseled away beneath an approved account of their disgrace. She carved those names into a new pillar without pretending their owners had been innocent. Smaller clans now gather behind her demand that the Khazad preserve the whole record, even when remembrance threatens a useful peace between powerful families.

Pale-lavender wrap robe with earth-ocher stone-carver's apron and soft plain cuffs. She chisels a fresh rune into a stone tablet with one hand while tracing the preceding carved line with the fingertips of the other; candlelit ancestral pillars, solemn tactile patience, no glowing eyes.

leaders.hand_activity: Chiseling a rune into a stone tablet while tracing the preceding carved line with the fingertips of her other hand.

leaders.name: Ordan Outledge
leaders.angle: Landless dwarves and mobile prospecting companies challenge the assumption that security begins with an established hold.
leaders.backstory: Ordan's family returned from prospecting to discover that their clan had sold its marginal homes to settle a larger house's debt. He gathered other dispossessed crews into a caravan that opened abandoned passes and lived from salvage, surveys, and armed escort. When neighboring lords imposed tolls, his companies seized the tollhouses and offered the same roads to everyone who paid for their upkeep. He seeks enough land to found a hold, but his followers fear that becoming respectable will mean shutting the gates on people like themselves.

leaders.hand_activity: Setting a survey compass on a mountain map and scratching a new pass route into it with a short iron point.

leaders.name: Sovna Trueweight
leaders.angle: The historical trauma of magical fraud produces transparent standards for outsiders, rather than isolation or retaliatory cheating.
leaders.backstory: Sovna trained as an assayer in a hold where an illusory shipment had ruined three generations of one family. Instead of forbidding foreign trade, she built testing rooms where dwarf and stranger could watch the same metal weighed, scratched, and checked against enchantment. Her publicly recorded standards attracted merchants excluded by clan monopolies and gave honest small traders a way to challenge richer rivals. The market towns have chosen her to lead them because she treats distrust as a problem to solve before a bargain, rather than a debt to collect afterward.

Emerald-green guild waistcoat over clean white rolled sleeves and a narrow assay apron. She rubs a coin across a black touchstone and points to the fresh metal streak with her other hand for a customer; open daylight testing booth, modest coin trays, candid meticulous assurance.

leaders.hand_activity: Rubbing a coin across a black touchstone while pointing to its fresh metal streak with her other hand for an unseen customer.

leaders.name: Velisar
leaders.angle: An immortal witness who spends the Sidar's accumulated memory on justice outside their borders.
leaders.backstory: Velisar became a shade to remember the names of a village that a victorious king ordered struck from every chronicle. Centuries later, she discovered that she could recall its tax rolls perfectly but no longer remember her sister's laugh. She now leads a company of witnesses who record testimony before fading can empty it of feeling, and brings their records into foreign courts even when Sandalphon's seclusion would be safer.

leaders.name: Nemeia
leaders.angle: Patient commerce and contractual memory instead of isolation or military guardianship.
leaders.backstory: Nemeia was a mortal factor hired to settle debts whose Sidar creditors had forgotten why they were owed. She learned to translate a shade's century-long patience into leases, warehouses and quiet purchases along the roads beyond the mist. Her trading houses now provision several hidden cities, and the shades accept her leadership because she alone can tell them which obligations still belong to the living.

leaders.name: Orven
leaders.angle: The living inhabitants of Sidar cities claim a political voice while retaining their immortal neighbors.
leaders.backstory: Orven kept the ferry to a hidden Sidar city long after its immortal council stopped noticing the villages on the opposite bank. When a flood drove those villagers to his landing, he opened the passage and housed them in districts that had stood empty for generations. The mortal households made him their speaker, and he persuades the Grey that a city can shelter new lives without surrendering the old ones it preserves.

leaders.name: Satha
leaders.angle: The wish to preserve a hidden city hardens into the coercive preservation of its inhabitants.
leaders.backstory: Satha once painted portraits so that newly faded shades could remember the faces they had surrendered. After raiders burned her gallery, she enclosed her district behind wards that admitted neither fire nor uninvited travelers. Her followers call it the safest place in Erebus, but she now forbids residents to leave and treats every change of loyalty, trade or family as damage to a collection entrusted to her care.

leaders.name: Terev
leaders.angle: A restless artisan sends Sidar retrieval expeditions into the world rather than waiting within it.
leaders.backstory: Terev chose fading so that death could never interrupt the mosaic he had spent half his life assembling. He returned from seclusion to find its missing panels displayed as trophies in the halls of three foreign dynasties. His fellow dispossessed artisans furnish a small army that steals their works back, while his refusal to ask who now treasures those works keeps restitution perilously close to conquest.

leaders.name: Maris Tallow
leaders.angle: Lighthouse keepers and harbor pilots build maritime authority around safe passage.
leaders.backstory: Maris lost her first ship because two rival captains extinguished a harbor beacon to settle a wager. She bought the ruined tower with her salvage share and persuaded neighboring keepers to answer one another's signals regardless of which flag approached. leaders.angle: The Lanun explore and study the changed sea instead of mastering it through piracy or surrendering to it.

He began paying divers and conjurers to measure the currents, ruins and strange voices that other captains dismissed as bad omens. leaders.angle: Lanun freedom expressed through a fleet of fiercely contractual shareholders and floating markets.

leaders.name: Torvek Antler-Crown
leaders.angle: Seasonal confederation and hunting law as an alternative to a single permanent pack tyrant.
leaders.backstory: Torvek survived three disastrous migrations by persuading rival packs to take different valleys rather than fight over the same dwindling herd. He established a seasonal moot where chiefs stake their hunting claims with antlers and surrender a share of the meat if they break their word. The agreement has made him wealthy in followers and obligations, though he owns no permanent hall and must win the moot's trust again each spring. He accepts raiding beyond the marked hunting grounds, but punishes a chief who starves another Doviello pack as severely as one who flees a duel.

He returned with hunters to break the remaining collars, then kept the freed prisoners under his own command until they had repaid him in service. His raiders now pursue priests and wizards across borders, taking their dependants as guarantees against retaliation. To Nask, Doviello freedom means that no sorcerer may hold his pack by the throat, and the safest way to ensure it is to put every sorcerer's household in his own fist first.

leaders.angle: Perpentach facet: a healer among his inner voices commands a breakaway court that treats his other personalities as usurpers of the same body.

At the next feast another voice revoked the decree, but three provincial circuses kept the first command and proclaimed the Gentle Witness their rightful sovereign. They shelter the king whenever his gentler facet prevails and dispatch his own signed letters to recruit soldiers against the courts obeying his other selves. The Witness calls those selves usurpers, even as they answer through his own mouth, and his followers fight to preserve a mercy their king may no longer remember promising.

His stagehands and merchants organised a court around those commands, then refused the Laughing Man's subsequent order to burn the accounts for a joke. They claim the Director alone speaks with royal authority and raise armies to bring the king's other courts back to their appointed places. The personality that savoured that silence founded the Empty Audience, a court of puppets and living courtiers who promise him peace if every troublesome self can be assigned a permanent role. Its ministers obey the king's commands when that facet is ascendant and treat his later pleas to release the captives as interference from the very usurpers they must imprison. leaders.name: Velisse the Understudy
leaders.angle: A demon summoned for a stage performance who escapes its binding, appropriates the mimic tradition, and builds an independent rival carnival court.

Her escaped performers and mimics now enter border towns in the uniforms of their expected defenders, then announce the arrival of an entirely new court. Velisse offers every captive a starring role in her expanding carnival, but keeps their true names and memories as payment so that no one else can ever cast them again.

leaders.angle: A goblin industrial constituency that treats Braduk's fire as productive infrastructure rather than a command to raid.

leaders.angle: A mortal Calabim administration that survives by preserving the fiction of an absent vampire lord.
